correctness.rationale: Setting D(y)=[1,y] in the compatibility identity gives [x,y]=2xD(y)−D(xy). Adding the swapped formula yields the Leibniz rule since 2 is invertible. Conversely, in the cyclic Jacobi sum for xD(y)−yD(x), the second-derivative terms cancel in pairs and so do the products of first derivatives; the extra derivative-of-multiplier terms cancel in transposed Leibniz. The derivation condition on t^4 is 4t³D(t)=0, imposing precisely zero constant coefficient also in characteristic 3. Surjectivity of a multiplication-preserving isomorphism forces it to preserve 1; t maps to ut+vt²+wt³ with u≠0, and these are all the automorphisms. The chain rule gives the conjugate coefficient f(φ(t))/φ′(t). Multiplying out to degree three gives the stated action, with the b-dependent terms cancelling in the cubic coefficient. For a≠0, v,w remove b,c, leaving q² points per fixed a; for a=0,b≠0 the complete invariant is c/b² with q−1 points per orbit; for a=b=0,c≠0 the square action has two equally sized orbits. Orbit-stabilizer with (q−1)q² automorphisms yields every stabilizer size and the mass sums to q³. This proof applies to all stated odd prime powers independent of finite regression examples.
residual_risks: The supplied reported finite experiments are prime-field examples; the extension-field and characteristic-three assertions rest on the general proof, not extrapolation.

value.rationale: This is an exact classification for a natural low-dimensional local algebra, not just a count of derivations or a complex normal-form list. It determines the finite-field distinction between algebraically closed and rational conjugacy in the cubic-leading stratum, identifies the quadratic-leading parameter, and gives the stabilizers needed for using the census as weighted isomorphism data, including in characteristic three.
residual_risks: No statement for higher truncations, ordinary Poisson structures, characteristic two or all four-dimensional associative types.
